channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: EU chief urges leaders to 'compromise' for budget deal by year-end
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa urged European leaders to seek compromise on the bloc's long-term budget at a summit Thursday, as Brussels pushes to lock in the plans before next year's French election where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is leading in opinion polls. "Now it is time for all of the leaders to participate in this debate with an open mind, a constructive approach, and a sense of compromise. Because we need to approve this budget timely. That means by the end of this year," Costa said. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels, Belgium.

item.title: French far-right leader Bardella faces fresh anti-Semitism accusations in media reports
item.description: French far-right leader ⁠Jordan Bardella faced fresh ​accusations of past antisemitic remarks on Thursday, as French media published an additional ​trove of comments purportedly made in chats from when he was a teenager in 2013. The initial allegations against Bardella, the president of the far-right National Rally party, were published ​by investigative outlet ‌Mediapart in September. It reported that he had made ⁠a slew of antisemitic and conspiratorial comments. Bardella denies making antisemitic remarks. FRANCE 24's French Politics Editor Marc Perelman tells us more.

item.title: Egypt: 31 people killed in Cairo after fuel truck overturns
item.description: A fire broke out on a busy highway in Egypt’s capital, Cairo, on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people after a fuel truck reportedly overturned. The suspected driver was arrested on Thursday, according to Egypt’s public prosecutor’s office.

item.title: Alleged Islamic State group propagandist Emily Konig on trial in France
item.description: Accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists, Emily Konig went on trial in Paris on Thursday. Originally from Brittany, Konig spent a decade in Syria before returning to France in 2022. She is charged with criminal association with a terrorist organisation and faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago is following the trial in Paris and joins us to explain the defence's strategy.

item.title: French media publish fresh claims of far-right leader Bardella's 'anti-Semitic torrent'
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, November 26: French media outlets Mediapart and Le Monde publish an additional trove of messages purporting to show far-right leader Jordan Bardella's rampant anti-Semitic thoughts as a young member of the party in 2013. Also: France holds the first trial of a female jihadist, Émilie König. Kilmar Abrego Garcia, once the face of Donald Trump's brutal mass deportations, arrives in Spain. Plus: we find out why the rich world is in the midst of a "sex recession."

item.title: France: Senior officials investigated over suspected leaks to far-right National Rally
item.description: Two senior figures in France have been caught up in an investigation into suspected leaks to the far-right National Rally. The prefect of the Loiret and former top official at the Interior Ministry, Hugues Moutouh, has been removed from his post after being suspected of passing on confidential information about investigations. A deputy prosecutor in Paris, who was found at the party's headquarters during a police search, is now also under administrative inquiry

item.title: EU Budget talks: France seeks to protect Common Agricultural Policy subsidies
item.description: Leaders from EU countries are meeting in Brussels on Thursday and Friday for another round of talks on the EU's next multi-year budget. For France, the main aim of the negotiations is to prevent a reduction in the funding allocated to the Common Agricultural Policy, a subsidy vital for French agriculture – a position Macron made clear in a meeting with farmers unions in Paris on Wednesday.

item.title: Trump unveils new tariffs on 14 trade partners over 'unfair' industrial capacity
item.description: US President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on Wednesday on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union, undeterred in his protectionist push by the losses his Republican Party suffered in US midterm elections. His administration proposed new maximum potential rates of 20% to 40% to counter excess industrial capacity that it says these countries are promoting.

item.title: 'King tide' waves batter California coast, soaking San Francisco
item.description: Massive waves carried on king tides battered California's coast Wednesday, prompting evacuations and soaking San Francisco, but sparing feared mass disruptions to Thanksgiving holiday travel. San Francisco already recorded its highest November water levels in more than 40 years on Tuesday morning, according to the National Weather Service.

item.title: WATCH: Man uses balloon art to pay off $400K in student loans
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a doctor in New York who's using his balloon twisting talents to help him pay off his student loan debt.

item.title: New York declares emergency as Thanksgiving storm threatens East Coast
item.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul's office declared a State of Emergency on Thanksgiving.

item.title: Iran live updates: IRGC claims 2 oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: 'Sacré sel': France's love of salt
item.description: We take a look at a salt scandal that is rocking the UK, after Maldon sea salt was found to come, in part, from rock salt imported from Germany. We also discuss France's relationship to salt (le sel) and the different kinds in France, from fleur de sel to sel gris. Finally, we look at French history and expressions about salt.

item.title: Thanksgiving Day store hours: Which stores are open and closed
item.description: See which national supermarket chains and stores will be staffed as usual and which ones will close for the Thanksgiving holiday.

item.title: 'Memories of a Good Meal': How food made a difference during WWII
item.description: New Orleans Chef Alon Shaya's new cookbook shares stories of resilience from World War II, centered around food.

item.title: At Albuquerque's Indian Pueblo Kitchen, Native American dishes are the main course
item.description: At an Albuquerque, N.M., museum, the restaurant is just as much of a draw as the exhibitions, with dishes like green chile stew and sweet biscochitos flavored with anise and cinnamon.

item.title: Dubai wholesaler plans renewed bid for collapsed Poundland
item.description: The Dubai-based businessman who emerged as a suitor for Poundland days before its collapse into insolvency is planning a fresh bid to buy the retailer out of administration.

item.title: Large explosion reported at a major oil facility in the Thai capital
item.description: An explosion has occurred at a major oil facility in Bangkok, prompting authorities to tell residents to evacuate

item.title: Le Pen's top ally Bardella faces fresh allegations of anti-semitic comments
item.description: French investigative outlet Mediapart on Thursday published extracts from private conversations in which far-right leader Jordan Bardella allegedly made anti-semitic remarks as a teenager, prompting fresh accusations that he has denied.

item.title: UK writes to veterans to ready them for possibility of mobilisation
item.description: The UK has written to around 100,000 former military personnel to ready them for the possibility of mobilisation in the event of war.

item.title: 'We are not fighting culture, we fight to end FGM: It's a human rights violation of women and girls'
item.description: “We fight to end FGM because it is a human rights violation of women and girls. We are not fighting culture.” Caroline Lagat, Legal Advisor at Equality Now’s Africa office in Nairobi, discusses the challenges of ending female genital mutilation (FGM) and child marriage. She points to insufficient funding, conflicting marriage laws and growing community resistance to campaigns against FGM. While acknowledging some progress, Lagat calls on the government to be "the face of the campaign to end FGM and child marriage.”

item.title: Injury-hit PSG drop first points of Champions League campaign against Roma
item.description: After kicking off their Champions League title defence with four consecutive wins, Luis Enrique's men were held to a draw at home by the Italian side Roma. Real Madrid are now two points clear at the top of the standings.

item.title: Huge explosion at oil depot in Bangkok sends fireball into sky
item.description: An explosion at an oil depot in Bangkok sent a large fireball and thick black smoke into the sky, journalists said Thursday, as local authorities urged people nearby to evacuate.

item.title: 'Biggest shake-up of stalking laws in over a decade' unveiled
item.description: A new standalone stalking offence is to be introduced as part of what the government is calling the "biggest shake-up of stalking laws in over a decade".

item.title: UK net migration falls to lowest level in three decades, excluding pandemic
item.description: UK net migration fell to 77,000 in the year to June 2026, provisional new data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) shows.

item.title: Aid cuts to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan further curb women's access to healthcare, education and food
item.description: Having lived and worked in Afghanistan for seven years, photojournalist Élise Blanchard offers an intimate account of what daily life is like for Afghan women today. Joining Genie Godula on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, she explains how restrictions vary across the country, depending on where women live, their families and the local enforcement of Taliban decrees. She stresses the need to maintain access to healthcare, primary education and food, pointing to severe cuts in humanitarian assistance by the US and EU.

item.title: 'Unacceptable': China, EU among major economies against new US tariffs
item.description: China, the European Union and other major trading partners on Thursday criticised new US tariffs of up to 20 percent proposed by US President Donald Trump after a probe into alleged global overcapacity, raising the prospect of fresh trade tensions with allies and rivals alike.

item.title: EU leaders face showdown over Ukraine funding as divisions deepen
item.description: European Union leaders on Thursday are set to tackle deep divisions as they meet in Brussels to discuss the bloc's long-term budget in Brussels, which includes a proposed €45 billion loan to keep Ukraine funded through 2027.

item.title: FCC says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists are skeptical
item.description: The Trump administration gave Elon Musk's SpaceX the green light to deploy 1 million satellites that it said would create data centers in space, a move that has raised skepticism among scientists.

item.title: Elon Musk pledges two SpaceX shares for every American child
item.description: Elon Musk says every child in the US will receive two shares in his space and AI company, SpaceX.

item.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
item.description: Taylor revealed his battle with Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer in 2022. He was the guitarist of the 1980s English band Duran Duran, whose pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf" and "Rio".

item.title: Iraqi court sentences 8 French nationals to life in prison for IS group membership
item.description: An Iraqi court sentenced eight French nationals to life in prison and two others to 15 years on Thursday for joining the Islamic State group, as Baghdad steps up prosecutions of thousands of alleged jihadists transferred from Syria.

item.title: Steelers cut Aaron Rodgers after the QB rips coach Mike McCarthy on TV
item.description: The move capped a chaotic 18 hours in which the team announced it was benching the 42-year-old future Hall of Famer for backup Mason Rudolph ahead of Friday's visit from Denver.

item.title: 'It's really outrageous': Women face violence in the streets and 'what we see online is even worse'
item.description: On the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, FRANCE 24's François Picard is pleased to welcome back Choralyne Dumesnil, an attorney practising in Paris and California, to discuss misogyny, sexual violence, cyberbullying and the challenges victims face in seeking justice. "There's always that stigma when you lodge a complaint. You get questioned, you get cross-examined," notes Picard. Despite efforts to raise awareness, Dumesnil sees little significant change in society.

item.title: Live: EU leaders meet in Brussels amid division over Ukraine funding
item.description: EU leaders are set to clash in Brussels on Thursday over a proposed €45 billion loan to fund Ukraine in 2027, with Germany pressing members to contribute and others seeking exemption. A day earlier, US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to escalate its war with Ukraine after talks in Florida. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: U.S. Judge rules FCC violated ABC's free speech rights to please Trump
item.description: A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. The stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets.

item.title: Major US tech index comes close to crashing into a bear market
item.description: A tech-heavy index on Wall Street briefly teetered into bear market territory on Wednesday - as AI-exposed stocks continue to face heavy sell-offs.

item.title: US authorises SpaceX to launch up to one million satellites for orbital data centres
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX's plan to deploy up to one million satellites to build data centres in orbit, giving Elon Musk's company a major foothold in the industry. The authorisation runs through 2040, as tech firms race to move computing infrastructure into space despite significant technical hurdles.

item.title: At least 31 killed in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns on busy highway
item.description: At least 31 people were killed and 15 injured when a fuel truck overturned and burst into flames on a busy highway in Cairo on Wednesday, engulfing nearby vehicles, Egyptian authorities said.

item.title: Powerful US storm forces historic postponement of New York's Thanksgiving Day Parade
item.description: A powerful storm forecast to bring fierce winds and heavy rain to the northeastern United States has forced the unprecedented postponement of the city's 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade, with the event rescheduled for Saturday. Officials warned that Thursday's conditions could bring down tree limbs and power lines, while posing a safety risk to the parade's giant balloons and the crowds below.

item.title: Britain's weather could be about to feel very different, Met Office warns
item.description: The UK can expect fewer winter frosts and more days of hot weather as a result of climate change, according to the Met Office.

item.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies aged 65
item.description: Andy Taylor, whose guitar riffs helped shape Duran Duran's distinctive sound and propel the British band to global fame in the 1980s, has died aged 65 after a long battle with prostate cancer, the band and his family said Wednesday.
